# Let the driver tell the step how far to go

[The final clock interval can be shorter than the requested timestep. The numerical update has to know that.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

This refactoring of `05_simulator` separates the time loop from a small
spectral heat update. The problem is one cosine mode,
$u(x,0)=1+.2\cos x$, repeated in the two transverse directions.
Its amplitude makes the effect of every accepted interval visible.

## Give the driver a step and three hooks

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="driver" dedent=4}
```

The native driver calls `start` once, performs an initial `save` when
due, then advances the clock before `apply`, `step` and any due `save`.
The two-argument step receives the current time and the actual clock
advance. `apply` is a place for time-dependent conditions; this example
records the hook without changing the field.

The default `dt: .07` and `end: .2` produce intervals .07,.07,.06.
For backward Euler, the mode's final amplitude is

$$
A=.2\prod_m(1+\Delta t_m)^{-1}.
$$ {#eq-amplitude}

Reusing a multiplier prepared for .07 on the last interval would be a
stable computation of the wrong elapsed time.

## A save request is not automatically a step boundary

`saveat: .1` supplies output opportunities to the fixed-step `Time`
driver; it does not split .07 steps at time .1. Read the actual
`save` rows in `results/events_rank_*.csv`. For explicit output-time
clipping and rejected attempts, compare
[the transactional clock lesson](../../integration/output-clock/index.qmd).

The historical one-argument step callback is also supported, but it
cannot see a clipped final interval. A fixed-dt method used through that
interface needs a run whose every interval really equals its private dt.

## Read the ledger and the field together

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
```

Each event records its hook, step, accepted time, interval and expected
discrete mode amplitude. `results/field_rank_*.csv` contains the actual
final owned field. The tests check the hook ordering, the clipped final
interval and every field sample on one and two ranks.

Try an end time shorter than `dt`, keeping `saveat` no greater than
that end time, then one that is an exact multiple.
Predict the multiplier product before running. Keep the
[source](model.cpp) and [input](input.json) together.
:::
